Article Title: 'Would have hanged myself if guilty': Brij Bhushan after acquittal in wrestlers' sexual harassment case
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on Monday said he "had complete faith that justice would be done" and "never felt guilty" after a Delhi court acquitted him in the sexual harassment case filed by women wrestlers.Reiterating that the case was a "conspiracy", the ex-BJP MP said he had maintained from the very beginning that he would "hang myself" if even one of the allegations against him was proved.His remarks came after Delhi's Rouse Avenue Court acquitted Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar in the case.Reacting to the verdict, Brij Bhushan said, "I said this was a conspiracy, and if any of the allegations against me are found to be true, I will hang myself. To this day, I've stood by that statement. Today, after almost three years, the court has honorably acquitted me and Vinod... I always stood up for those who were weak, those whose rights were violated.""I had complete faith that justice would be done to me, and I never felt guilty... We were fighting for the junior athletes whose rights were being violated, and I am happy that we won that fight," he added.Referring to the court's verdict, the former WFI chief further noted, "The honourable judge said that Brij Bhushan Singh and Vinod Tomar are acquitted with honour.From the very first day, I had said that if even a single allegation against me was proved, I would be ready to face the harshest punishment."He further noted, "I have not just been acquitted, I have been acquitted with honour... Struggle brings refinement... I have nothing to say to those who were against me."Calling the verdict a "moment of happiness", he added, "Today, the court has acquitted us with honour and it is a matter of happiness for me. What I had said on the first day has turned out to be true. I did not know what the other side was thinking, but my first reaction was that the truth would prevail. Today is a moment of happiness."Brij Bhushan also quoted a verse from the Ramcharitmanas after the judgment saying, "होइहि सोइ जो राम रचि राखा।" (What is meant to be will be, as destined by Lord Ram.)The case stemmed from allegations made by six women wrestlers, following which Delhi Police filed a chargesheet against the former BJP MP on June 15, 2023. He was charged under sections 354 (assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 354A (sexual harassment), 354D (stalking) and 506 (criminal intimidation) of the Indian Penal Code.Following protests by the wrestlers at Delhi's Jantar Mantar in 2023, Delhi Police registered an FIR and later filed a nearly 1,500-page chargesheet against Brij Bhushan, invoking provisions related to sexual harassment, assault or criminal force against a woman, stalking and criminal intimidation under the Indian Penal Code.Tomar was also named as a co-accused.After hearing final arguments from both the prosecution and the defence, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Ashwani Panwar had reserved the judgment last month. The proceedings were conducted in a closed courtroom, and August 3 was fixed for pronouncement of the verdict.During the trial, the court heard submissions from senior advocate Rebecca John, appearing for the complainants, while the defence was led by advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati. The court also examined members of the Special Investigation Team (SIT) and the investigating officer before delivering its verdict.
Article Summary: Former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh acquitted in sexual harassment case. Delhi's Rouse Avenue Court acquitted Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar. Case stemmed from allegations made by six women wrestlers, following which Delhi Police filed a chargesheet against the former BJP MP.

Article Title: A race to save 23 sperms, and a teen cancer survivor’s chance at fatherhood
Article Text:
After hours of meticulous search, there was success

A childhood condition

When every routine option failed

A

race

against the clock

Twenty-three shots at fatherhood

For a 19-year-old battling testicular cancer, survival was only one part of the fight. The other was far more personal.After surgeons removed his only remaining testis, a team of 10 specialists at Mumbai’s Sir H N Reliance Foundation Hospital came together on July 25, 2026 with a singular mission — to comb through the nearly dead organ to finding any surviving sperms.While the surgery to remove the testis was lifesaving, it threatened to end the teenager’s (his identity has been withheld on family’s request) chance of becoming a biological father.The odds that the team of surgeons, urologists, andrologists, fertility specialists and embryologists would find any surviving sperms in the surgically removed testis were daunting. But after hours of meticulous search, there was success — they found 23 viable sperms. The cells were frozen and preserved for future use. What had begun as an attempt to save a life, ended with the hope of a new one taking birth sometime in the future.The teen’s medical journey had begun long before his cancer diagnosis. He was born with cryptorchidism (undescended testes) — a condition in which both testes fail to descend into the scrotum before birth and remain inside the abdomen.Since the testes require a cooler environment for normal sperm production, the condition can impair fertility and is also associated with an increased risk of testicular cancer.When he was just a year old, he underwent orchiopexy, a procedure to bring the testes into the scrotum. However, one testis had already sustained irreversible damage and had to be removed. The other was successfully brought down into the scrotum.Some years later, this surviving testis developed swelling. Investigations revealed a large tumour that had affected nearly 95% of the organ. Removing the cancerous testis became essential to save his life. But for the teenager, the surgery carried a devastating consequence — it would permanently end his body’s ability to produce sperms. “His case was extremely challenging. We wanted to explore every possible option to preserve his fertility and give him a chance of biological fatherhood,” said Dr Firuza Parikh, director of IVF at Well Women and Men’s Centre, Sir H N Reliance Foundation Hospital.Before the surgery, the patient provided two semen samples. Both were analysed using an advanced AI-assisted sperm detection system.“We have the latest technology to search for sperm in cryptozoospermia — a condition in which sperm are present in extremely low numbers and may not be detected during routine semen analysis, requiring microscopic examination to find them. The technology, the first of its kind in India, was developed in collaboration with the AZ-VUB IVF team in Belgium,” Dr Parikh explained.Yet, despite the advanced analysis, the results brought heartbreaking news — not a single sperm could be located in the two samples. This medical condition is called azoospermia, meaning a person ejaculates a normal-looking fluid, but the fluid contains zero sperm cells.“This was a major setback for us, the family was devastated... now the only option left was to attempt Onco-TESE (oncological testicular sperm extraction) — a specialised fertility preservation technique used in cancer patients,” she said.The team decided to attempt a rare “ex-vivo Onco-TESE”, a procedure in which sperm retrieval is performed after the cancer-affected testis has been surgically removed. The organ is examined outside the body in a controlled laboratory environment to identify any surviving sperm-producing tissue untouched by the tumour.On July 25, surgical oncologists Dr Raman Deshpande and Dr Soumil Vyas removed the cancer-affected testis. Now, the team had just five to six hours to locate and extract the sperms.A team led by consultant andrologists Dr Rupin Shah and Dr Himanshu Gohil dissected small pieces of tissue surrounding the tumour in search of any surviving tissue. The doctors relied on ultrasound and MRI scans to guide them towards the tiny regions that might still contain viable tissue.These healthy tissues were then sent to the hospital’s IVF laboratory. “Healthy tissue fractions were carefully separated. Once the required tissue fractions were identified, they were placed in a specialised sterile transport medium to maintain tissue viability and preserve any potential viable sperm cells. Prompt processing is critical, as it provides the best chance of preserving any surviving sperm cells. ”Embryologists led by Dr Varsha Kuril spent five hours going through the tissues for signs of surviving sperms. When the team identified the first viable sperm cell, they knew they were onto a special moment in medical history. By the time they were done, the team had identified 23 sperms, which were then cryopreserved.“Twenty-three may sound like a disappointingly small number in the world of sperm counts, where a healthy male can produce millions of sperm cells. But in this case, every single one was a victory — each cell represented a possibility that cancer had nearly taken away,” said Dr Parikh, adding that doctors “will wait for the time when this young boy gets married and wishes to have children.Then the sperm will be thawed and used for IVF. ”According to Dr Tarang Gianchandani, chief executive officer of the hospital, the procedure marked a significant milestone for the institution. “We have been freezing eggs and ovarian tissue in women with cancer for a long time, but this was the first time that we could get testicular tissue from a testis that was almost entirely destroyed by cancer. And we succeeded only because of our team’s efforts,” she said.

Article Title: PM Modi: I forgive those who abused me & my mother, our job to guide them
Article Text:

Mistakes happen at a young age, says PM Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said on Friday he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother, saying they are misguided children and it is “our job to show them the right way”.In a video message, Modi said punishing these youth and making them run around courts will not change circumstances, adding that these children have lost their way and must be guided instead of being subjected to any harassment. His comments came amid incidents of criminal cases being lodged against some young protesters for abusing him during the recent student protest. “Everybody saw what happened at Jantar Mantar,” the PM said.They abused not only me but also my late mother. It was such a vile thing. But I want to say today that mistakes happen at a young age, and this is also the opportunity to correct those mistakes,” he said. “I want to forgive them. Society should also accept my decision,” he said in a clear indication that cases against these youngsters will be withdrawn. Modi as Gujarat CM had forgiven a youngster accused of sending a threatening mail to him, sources said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi said on Friday he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother. He said punishing these youth and making them run around courts will not change circumstances. His comments came amid incidents of criminal cases being lodged against some young protesters for abusing him.

Article Title: Youth quitting drugs real warriors: PM on national drive
Article Text:
PM Modi called for rejecting stigma on the issue. “Youth who come out fighting addiction are not weak; they are real warriors,” he said.

Give drug survivors a second chance, respect them: PM Modi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Drugs can give a momentary high but family and professional lives will hit a low, PM Modi told youth in a warning against substance abuse on Sunday, and exhorted families not to hide any addiction in the name of social prestige but reach out to experts and cultivate a culture of frank communication with kids.Launching ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’ (campaign for drug-free youth for developed India), Modi called for rejecting stigma on the issue. “Youth who come out fighting addiction are not weak; they are real warriors,” he said.PM Modi said society should instead respect those who overcome their drug addiction. “They are real warriors whose incredible courage is their true identity,” he said in a virtual address, with a host of chief ministers, governors, spiritual figures and a large number of youngsters joining the event from across the country.As the nation has set the goal of ‘Viksit Bharat’, it is imperative that the country’s youth remain physically and mentally fit, steering clear of destructive habits like drugs, he said, stressing the importance of support system offered by the society besides the help from yoga and meditation.He said, “Even if a youth has mistakenly fallen into the trap of addiction, it absolutely does not mean that all doors are closed for them.”Society should respect them, embrace them and give them a second chance, he said.Substance abuse has long been a serious concern in parts of the north-east and Punjab, where it has become a major plank for all political parties in the run-up to elections early next year.Modi noted enemy countries use the supply of drugs as part of their terror plans because they know that youth are the future of country.The campaign will continue for the next 100 weeks, and every Sunday, activities related to art, culture, sports, meditation, spirituality and services will be organised to take the message of de-addiction to new people.Family members live with this pain every day, watching their children gradually lose themselves before their eyes, he said. Strict action is being taken against drug traffickers across the country. The arrests have gone up several times, and drugs worth thousands of crores of rupees have been seized, the PM said.
Article Summary: PM Modi calls for rejecting stigma on the issue. “Youth who come out fighting addiction are not weak; they are real warriors,” he said. ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’ (campaign for drug-free youth for developed India)

NEW DELHI: Former BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla on Sunday took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi over his Friendship Day message for Gen Z, referring to the Korean finger heart emoji in the Congress MP's social media post as “counting fingers”, accusing the Gandhi family and the grand old party of corruption.Poonawalla, a former Congress spokesperson, resigned from the BJP in a surprise move on Friday. He has frequently targeted Rahul Gandhi since leaving the Congress.“No, no, no, don’t mistake it for the Korean heart gesture shared on Friendship Day,” Poonawalla said in a video posted on X, claiming that the gesture was “nothing new” for Rahul Gandhi and the Congress.“Rahul Gandhi ji said, ‘Still a student, learning something new every day.’ But this is not a new gesture for him. This is not a Korean heart... this is counting fingers,” he remarked, placing a few currency notes between his fingers to mimic the Korean finger heart gesture.He continued: “Counting corruption every day. Taking corruption bribes every day. The Gandhi family has more than an apprenticeship in this — they have a PhD. Ask the Karnataka government... ‘counting fingers.’ Happy Friendship Day.”Earlier in the day, Rahul Gandhi, in an apparent attempt to connect with Gen Z, posted a photo on Instagram and wrote: “Still a student, still learning something new every day. Today’s lesson: it’s Friendship Day and this 🫰 is a heart. Happy Friendship Day, everyone. Lots of love!”In the photo, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is seen wearing his trademark white shirt and making the popular Korean finger heart gesture.The Wayanad MP has increasingly used social media to engage with younger audiences in recent years.The outreach comes at a time when student and youth issues have gained renewed political attention, including after recent protests in Delhi that culminated in the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.

Article Title: 'That hurts us': CWG silver medalist Lovlina flags 'missing' Northeast on Glasgow restaurant's India map
Article Text:
CWG silver medallist Lovlina objects to 'missing' Northeast on Glasgow restaurant's napkins (Image/PTI,X)

(with inputs from PTI)

NEW DELHI: Commonwealth Games silver medallist and Assam boxer Lovlina Borgohain said she felt 'hurt' after noticing that the Northeast was missing from a map printed on napkins and displayed outside a popular Indian restaurant in Glasgow.The restaurant owners acknowledged the mistake and assured the Indian boxing contingent that it would be corrected.The incident took place when the Indian boxing team visited Mister Singh's India, The Home of Curry for a celebratory dinner after securing a record 10 medals, seven gold and three silver, at the Commonwealth Games.Lovlina noticed that the restaurant's branding showed an incomplete map of India without the Northeast. She immediately raised the issue with the management.Addressing the restaurant management during an interaction, Lovlina said the omission was upsetting."Please don't take this the wrong way. I felt a little hurt by this. In the map of India, our North East is missing. Yes, even outside, the map that's displayed has cut off the North East. As someone from the North East, that really hurts us. That's all I wanted to say.Please keep this in mind next time. Thank you so much," she said.Boxing Federation of India (BFI) president Ajay Singh, who was present at the restaurant, said there was no confrontation and that the issue was resolved amicably."There was no confrontation. It was an aberration and we pointed that out, me and Lovlina. They accepted their mistake and assured us that it will be corrected," Singh told PTI.The restaurant is a popular Indian dining destination in Glasgow and has hosted several visiting sports teams and dignitaries over the years.Lovlina won a silver medal in the women's 75kg boxing event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.The Tokyo Olympic bronze medallist lost a closely fought final to Australia's Emma-Sue Greentree by a 4-1 split decision, missing out on her first Commonwealth Games gold medal.The silver was Lovlina's maiden Commonwealth Games medal after earlier exits at Gold Coast 2018 and Birmingham 2022.India's boxing team has produced its best-ever Commonwealth Games campaign, winning a record seven gold and three silver medals. Overall, India has collected 35 medals at the Glasgow Games: 11 gold, 16 silver and eight bronze to occupy fourth place in the medal standings.
Article Summary: Assam boxer Lovlina Borgohain objects to'missing' Northeast on Glasgow restaurant's napkins. Incident took place when Indian boxing team visited Mister Singh's India, The Home of Curry for a celebratory dinner. The restaurant owners acknowledged the mistake and assured the Indian boxing contingent that it would be corrected.

Article Title: "When I think of love, I think about...": Hailee Steinfeld just revealed the one thing Josh Allen does that makes her forget new-mom exhaustion
Article Text:
Josh Allen surprised Hailee Steinfeld with roses mid-week (Getty Images)

Why did Josh Allen's surprise mean so much to Hailee Steinfeld?

Life has changed quickly for Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen and his wife, Hailee Steinfeld . After getting married earlier this year, the couple welcomed their daughter, Harper Haize Allen, in April and have been adjusting to the demands of first-time parenthood. Even with sleepless nights and busy schedules, Steinfeld says the small moments between them continue to matter most. In a personal essay for Vogue, the actress offered a rare look inside their home life, sharing how one thoughtful gesture from Allen reminded her that romance does not have to disappear once a couple becomes parents.Hailee Steinfeld's essay, published on July 28, explored the scents that have shaped different chapters of her life. The piece also marked her partnership with Estée Lauder as the face of its new fragrance, Glimmer. Rather than simply promoting the perfume, she used the opportunity to reflect on memories tied to smell, love and family.One story stood out above the rest."When I think of love, I think about a few Tuesdays ago, when my husband, Josh, came home, hugged me—a comforting musk that instantly puts me at ease—and then pulled from behind his back a bouquet of red roses wrapped in brown butcher paper and twine," she wrote.For many couples, flowers are a familiar gift. For Steinfeld, these roses carried far more meaning. She explained that they immediately brought back memories of the place where they chose to begin their married life together.The actress recalled visiting their wedding venue in Montecito, California, where the surroundings made an instant impression on both of them.She wrote that roses "will always remind me of our wedding in Montecito, California. We toured the venue holding hands, walking through the rose gardens, past the lemon trees and sprawling pink bougainvillea, and knew immediately that it was our place."That memory arrived during a period when daily life has been filled with work commitments and the responsibilities of raising a newborn. Instead of an elaborate celebration, Allen's simple surprise gave her a brief pause from the pace of new motherhood. It also reflected something many new parents often discover: meaningful gestures do not need to be grand to leave a lasting impact.Steinfeld also turned her attention to the newest member of their family. Writing about Harper, she reflected on how scent creates some of the earliest bonds between a parent and child, even before memories fully take shape."Someday Harper will know my smell, the faint smell of my perfume," she wrote. "That thought made me so excited to partner with Estée Lauder for its new perfume, Glimmer. It’s the first perfume I’ve ever worn that truly smells like me."While Allen prepares for another demanding NFL season with the Bills, Steinfeld's reflections offer a glimpse beyond football headlines. Her story is less about celebrity and more about the quiet routines that often define family life. In the middle of sleepless nights and changing priorities, she suggests that love is sometimes expressed in the simplest ways, through a familiar embrace, a bouquet of roses and memories that continue to grow alongside a young family.
Article Summary: Josh Allen surprised Hailee Steinfeld with roses mid-week. The couple welcomed their daughter, Harper Haize Allen, in April. Steinfeld's essay explored the scents that have shaped different chapters of her life. She also marked her partnership with Estée Lauder as the face of its new fragrance.

Article Title: 'I gave up': Tejaswin Shankar's emotional confession after turning CWG heartbreak into historic bronze
Article Text:
Tejaswin Shankar celebrates after winning the bronze medal in the men's decathlon event. (PTI Photo)

ALSO READ:

'I questioned everything'



From despair to historic bronze



'Your belief carried me'



Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: There were tears after one jump. Days later, there was history, a medal and a message that resonated far beyond the athletics track.Indian decathlete Tejaswin Shankar has opened up on the emotional turmoil he endured at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, revealing that he briefly "gave up" after a recurring knee injury shattered his hopes in the high jump before he picked himself up to script history with India's first-ever Commonwealth Games medal in the decathlon.The national record holder shared a deeply personal message on social media after returning home with a bronze medal, admitting the journey from heartbreak to the podium was one of the toughest tests of his career."There are moments in life when you feel like everything you've worked for is slipping away. This week, I had one of those moments," Tejaswin wrote.The 27-year-old had travelled to Glasgow hoping to defend the bronze medal he won in the high jump at the Birmingham Commonwealth Games in 2022 — India's first-ever medal in the event.Instead, his campaign unravelled almost instantly.A long-standing battle with chronic patellar tendinitis, commonly known as jumper's knee, resurfaced after his very first attempt in the high jump, forcing him to withdraw from the competition.The sight of Tejaswin crouching alone on the track, struggling to hold back tears, became one of the defining images of India's campaign.Those tears, however, were not because of physical pain."I’m going to be honest and admit for a while, I gave up," he revealed. "I questioned everything. I wondered if all the preparation had been for nothing."For any elite athlete, such moments can define a career. But for Tejaswin, they became the beginning of an extraordinary comeback.Instead of allowing disappointment to consume him, Tejaswin slowly rebuilt himself over the next few days."But somewhere along the way, I picked myself back up piece by piece. I was shattered emotionally but kept lying to myself that I was fine. One conversation, one treatment session, one event, one lap at a time," he added.Competing through pain, the Indian produced a remarkable performance across the gruelling two-day decathlon to finish with 7,976 points and claim the bronze medal — the first ever by an Indian in the event at the Commonwealth Games.It also marked his second Commonwealth Games medal after the high jump bronze in Birmingham four years ago.After clinching the historic podium finish, Tejaswin walked into the mixed zone with a smile replacing the tears seen earlier in the week."Guys, I won't cry today," he joked.The bronze was all the more remarkable considering he had entered the final 1,500m in third place and held on under immense physical and mental pressure to secure the medal.Reflecting on his remarkable turnaround, Tejaswin credited the people around him for helping him rediscover belief when he had lost faith in himself."Looking back, I realize I didn't do it alone. To my coaches, medical team, teammates, family, friends, sponsors, and every single person who called, messaged, or reached out on social media… thank you. Your belief carried me when I was struggling very hard to believe in myself," he wrote.The athlete also reflected on the deeper lessons sport continues to teach."Sport has a funny way of testing you. Sometimes it isn't about being the strongest or the most talented. Sometimes it's simply about refusing to stay down.""Proud to leave the Commonwealth Games with a bronze medal around my neck. It wasn't the path I imagined, but it taught me more than an easy victory ever could," he added.With Glasgow behind him, Tejaswin has already shifted his focus to the next challenge. Asian Games , see you soon. The Beast Never Stops," he concluded.
Article Summary: Indian decathlete Tejaswin Shankar has opened up on the emotional turmoil he endured at the 2026 Commonwealth Games. The 27-year-old revealed that he briefly "gave up" after a recurring knee injury shattered his hopes in the high jump. But he picked himself up to script history with India's first-ever Commonwealth Games medal in the decathlon.

Article Title: After historic CWG gold, Mirabai Chanu declares Asian Games 'make-or-break'
Article Text:
Mirabai Chanu (Image credit: X)

NEW DELHI: There is little left for Saikhom Mirabai Chanu to conquer at the Commonwealth Games.A record-extending third consecutive CWG gold medal in Glasgow has only strengthened her status as the undisputed queen of Commonwealth weightlifting. Add the silver she won in her debut Games in 2014, and Mirabai now stands as the most successful weightlifting athlete in CWG history.Yet, less than 24 hours after standing atop the podium once again, the Tokyo Olympic silver medallist had already turned the page."The very next day after winning gold, I started preparing for the Asian Games . I started training the next day itself," Mirabai told TOI upon her return to India on Sunday afternoon.For the 32-year-old, the celebrations are over. The focus has shifted completely to the one medal that has remained painfully out of reach throughout her glittering career — an Asian Games podium finish."The upcoming Games in Japan are very important for me. I don't have an Asiad medal and I want to win one. Before every Asiad, I have either suffered an injury or something has happened because of which I missed out on a medal.This time I have to overcome that. My focus is purely on the event. That's the one title I desperately want to win," she said.Having carried Indian weightlifting on her shoulders for more than a decade while battling recurring injuries, Mirabai knows opportunities are becoming increasingly precious."I am not thinking whether this will be my last Asiad or not. But I will compete like this is the best opportunity I have to win a medal...like this is the only Asiad I have. Future competitions can wait. Right now, the Aich-Nagoya Games offers me the best chance. For me, it is a make-or-break moment."Those words carry the weight of a career shaped as much by injuries as medals.The build-up to Glasgow was anything but straightforward. Mirabai won gold at the National Championships in Modinagar in Feb, setting national records in the process, but picked up a shoulder injury during the competition. The setback forced her to miss the Asian Championships as she stepped away from competition for months to allow her body to recover.Her comeback, however, was vintage Mirabai.Competing in Glasgow after months away from the platform, she comfortably lifted a Games record total of 190kg — 85kg in snatch and 105kg in clean and jerk — to clinch India's first gold of this edition of the Games. More importantly, she achieved what no other weightlifter has managed before by winning three successive CWG gold.It was the performance of a champion who understood the bigger picture.Mirabai admitted she deliberately avoided exhausting herself in Glasgow, preserving both her body and energy for the much bigger challenge that awaits in Japan."I preserved myself during the CWG. My focus was always on the Asiad. Now I have to improve my performance level. The competition there will be much tougher."That challenge will be formidable. Olympic champion Hou Zhihui of China, the powerful North Korean lifters and Thailand's Surodchana Khambao are likely to headline a world-class field where every kilogram can separate the medal winners from the rest."I have to train harder. China, North Korea and Thailand have very strong weightlifters. I need to raise my performance several notches. I have to prepare more and train harder."Unlike previous major championships, Mirabai will remain in India for the final phase of her preparations under long-time coach Vijay Sharma."There isn't much time before the Games. We cannot go abroad now. I will train here in India under Vijay sir. I will follow the same routine as I do before every major championship. Nothing special, but my performance level has to improve."Years of competing at the highest level have also taught Mirabai to respect her body's limits."I understand my body much better now. I know how my mind and body react. I have learnt from injuries and experience. That understanding is very important."Beyond the Games lies another major transition. With the International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) scrapping the women's 49kg division for the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, Mirabai will eventually have to move up to the new 53kg category — another challenge in an already extraordinary career.But that is a story for another day. For now, India's most decorated Commonwealth weightlifter has only one destination in mind. "This Games is the biggest moment for me. I have to come back with a medal at any cost. I don't want to let this opportunity go."
Article Summary: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu won a record-extending third consecutive CWG gold medal in Glasgow. The 32-year-old now stands as the most successful weightlifting athlete in CWG history. The Tokyo Olympic silver medallist had already turned the page.

Article Title: 'Vozinha! Vozinha!': FIFA World Cup breakout star gets hero's welcome in Chile after three delays
Article Text:
Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha arrives at the airport ahead of a move to Colo-Colo in Santiago, Chile. (AP Photo)

Three delays before dream move finally became reality



World Cup hero earns special jersey exception

One of the biggest breakout stars of the 2026 FIFA World Cup has finally arrived in Chile — and the reception was nothing short of extraordinary.Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, whose remarkable performances at the World Cup captured the imagination of football fans across the globe, landed in Santiago on Sunday to complete his move to Chilean giants Colo Colo after his arrival was delayed on three separate occasions.Hundreds of jubilant supporters gathered at Santiago's airport with flags, banners, drums and chants, turning the veteran goalkeeper's arrival into a celebration usually reserved for legends. Videos of the emotional welcome quickly spread across social media, underlining the popularity Vozinha has earned since his unforgettable World Cup campaign."I’m very happy to be here. And I want to thank the fans for the patience they’ve shown while waiting for me," the 40-year-old told reporters shortly after landing. "See you at the Monumental Stadium."Colo Colo, Chile's most successful football club, announced the signing of Josimar Évora Dias — better known worldwide as Vozinha — on July 24.However, what was expected to be a straightforward transfer soon became a complicated saga.Documentation issues and personal matters delayed the goalkeeper's arrival three different times, raising concerns among supporters eagerly waiting to welcome their new signing.The uncertainty finally ended on Sunday evening when Vozinha landed in Santiago at 8:35 p.m. local time to a rousing reception from hundreds of Colo Colo fans.The veteran is scheduled to undergo medical examinations before signing an initial six-month contract with an option to extend it by another year. He is expected to begin training with his new teammates on Tuesday before being officially unveiled by the club.Vozinha's move has already prompted an unprecedented rule change in Chilean football.The Chilean Football Federation unanimously voted to amend its regulations and allow the goalkeeper to wear "Vozinha" on the back of his jersey instead of his surname.Under previous league rules, players were required to display only their family names on their shirts.The exception reflects the global recognition attached to the nickname that became synonymous with Cape Verde's historic World Cup journey.Vozinha — whose nickname means "grandma" in Portuguese — became one of the tournament's most celebrated players after helping Cape Verde make history on their World Cup debut.At 40, he became the oldest player to feature in a nation's first-ever World Cup match and earned worldwide admiration with a string of spectacular saves against Spain, Uruguay and Argentina. His heroic display against eventual champions Spain, where he kept them scoreless, transformed him into one of the faces of the tournament.His popularity exploded during the competition. Before the World Cup, Vozinha had fewer than 50,000 Instagram followers. By the end of the tournament, that figure had soared beyond 29.5 million.For Colo Colo supporters, the excitement extends well beyond social media fame.Fans hope the experienced goalkeeper can inspire the Chilean league leaders to another domestic title before leading their challenge in next season's Copa Libertadores.
Article Summary: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha lands in Chile to complete move to Colo Colo. The 40-year-old became one of the biggest breakout stars of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. His arrival at Santiago's airport was met by hundreds of jubilant fans.

NEW DELHI: India ended their Commonwealth Games 2026 campaign in Glasgow on a high, finishing fourth in the medal standings with 39 medals - 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.Australia topped the medal table with 62 gold medals, followed by England (26) and Canada (18).Boxing was India's biggest success story. Indian boxers won 10 medals, including a record seven gold and three silver, to finish on top of the boxing medal table. The only other gold medal on the final day came from Soman Rana, who won the men's F57 para shot put title.India enjoyed its best-ever boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games.The women's team led the way by winning five gold medals. World champion Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Asian Games medallist Preeti Pawar (54kg), Asian champion Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) finished on top of the podium. Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg event.In the men's competition, Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (70kg) claimed gold medals. Jadumani Singh (55kg) and Asian Games bronze medallist Narender Berwal (+90kg) settled for silver.India's previous best boxing performance at the Commonwealth Games came in Gold Coast in 2018, when the team won seven medals, including three gold.India also enjoyed its best-ever Commonwealth Games in judo.Unnati Sharma added a bronze medal in the women's 63kg event after defeating South Africa's Skye Knoester by ippon in just one minute and seven seconds in the bronze-medal contest.She had lost to Australia's Saya Middleton in the semifinal but bounced back to finish on the podium.The bronze took India's judo medal tally to four, the country's best at the Commonwealth Games.Harsh Singh (men's -60kg) and Asmita Dey (women's -48kg) created history by becoming India's first-ever Commonwealth Games judo gold medallists. Yamini Mourya won silver in the women's -57kg category.Harsh Tokas narrowly missed a bronze medal in the men's -81kg event after losing to Australia's Keishin Ochi by ippon. Inunganbi Takhellambam (women's -70kg) and Karanjit Singh Maan (men's -90kg) were knocked out after losing their repechage bouts.India had several standout performances in athletics.Soman Rana won gold in the men's F57 para shot put with a season-best throw of 13.40m, while Shubham Juyal made it an Indian one-two by taking silver with 13.28m.Gulveer Singh created history by becoming the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the men's 5000m. He took bronze in the event after earlier winning silver in the men's 10,000m, making him the first Indian track and field athlete to win two individual medals at a single Commonwealth Games.India also celebrated a double podium finish in the men's triple jump. Praveen Chithravel won silver with 16.58m, while Selva Prabhu Thirumaran claimed bronze with 16.52m.Ramesh Shanmugam finished seventh in the men's T54 1500m para final. Priyanka Goswami finished seventh in the women's 10,000m race walk with a season-best time of 45:53.93, while Ravina was disqualified.In the men's pole vault, Dev Kumar Meena finished fourth with 5.30m and Kuldeep Kumar placed sixth with 5.10m.India's para athletes enjoyed their best-ever Commonwealth Games.The 28-member para contingent finished with seven medals - three gold, two silver and two bronze - matching the total number of medals India had won across all previous Commonwealth Games editions.Para track and field athletes won six medals - three gold, two silver and one bronze - while Jhandu Kumar added a bronze medal in para powerlifting.

Article Title: Draw inspiration from Tilak’s life to contribute for nation-building, Shah tells youth
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah confers Lokmanya Tilak National Award on NSA Ajit Doval in the presence of chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, and deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, in Pune on Saturday

Pune:

Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday urged the country’s youth to draw inspiration from freedom fighter Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s life to contribute for nation-building.Calling Lokmanya Tilak the tallest figure in the freedom struggle movement, Shah said, “Along with the freedom struggle movement, Tilak stressed on achieving self-reliance, discipline and sense of responsibility towards the nation. The younger generation should follow the life of Lokmanya Tilak to draw inspiration and contribute towards nation-building.”Shah on Saturday gave away the Lokmanya Tilak National Award to national security adviser (NSA) Ajit Doval at a ceremony in Pune. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , both the deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, president of Lokmanya Tilak Smarak Trust Rohit Tilak and others attended the award ceremony.Mentioning Tilak’s literary work of “Gita Rahasya”, Shah said, “Tilak’s literature will never be outdated. It remains eternal. If the youth of the country read Gita through Tilak’s point of view, they will never commit any mistake.”Congratulating Doval on receiving the Tilak national award, Shah said the first appointment Narendra Modi made after becoming the Prime Minister in 2014 was that of Doval as the NSA. “Under PM Modi’s leadership, India’s defence and foreign policies were strengthened, and Doval played an important role in shaping these policies.Doval is India’s longest serving NSA. The internal and external security of the country transformed under his tenure,” Shah said.“The Multi Agency Centre (MAC) has become the backbone of the country’s internal security under the Modi-led government and the strong foundation of MAC was laid by Doval as its founding chairman. When the history of Modi’s tenure would be written and an assessment would be made of the country’s internal and external security, a golden page about Doval would be included in it,” Shah said.Doval in his speech urged the country’s youth to sacrifice their personal interest and devote life to nation building. “We have got the window of opportunity to contribute to build the nation, which today’s youth should not let go. Remembering the sacrifices of our freedom fighters in the country’s freedom movement, the youth of the country should also dedicate their life to take the nation to new heights,” he said.Cautioning the youth regarding the challenges before the country, Doval said, “While India is on a path of development, not all are happy with our progress. Some people and countries are threatened by India’s development. Some internal and external challenges still persist before the country. The young generation should stand up to take on those challenges.”Doval said the country’s growth had been expedited under the leadership of PM Modi and home minister Shah, who never showed any hesitation in taking some tough decisions in the interest of the country. “India still has not reached its goal but we are fortunate to have a strong leadership of Modi and Shah, who ensured that people of the country get a conducive atmosphere to achieve its goal,” Doval added.Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said the combination of Modi, Shah’s leadership and Doval’s expertise in national security had transformed India’s image as a stronger nation in the entire world. He said, “Due to the efforts of Modi, Shah and Doval, we have sent a strong message to the entire world that India cannot be bullied anymore and in case of any threat, we can proactively respond by entering into the enemy’s territory also. ”Shah also paid floral tributes to the statue of Annabhau Sathe near Sarasbaug.
Article Summary: Amit Shah on Saturday gave away the Lokmanya Tilak National Award to national security adviser (NSA) Ajit Doval at a ceremony in Pune. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar also attended the award ceremony.

Article Title: 'I have a lot of respect for her': Pakistan's first female CWG boxing medallist credits Mary Kom for inspiring her
Article Text:
Mary Kom

Growing up in Pakistan's Punjab province, Fatima Zahra had few female boxing role models in her own country. She found one across the border in India's MC Mary Kom, whose journey inspired her to take up the sport and eventually become Pakistan's first female Commonwealth Games boxing medallist.The 22-year-old from Sargodha in Pakistan's Punjab province won a bronze medal in the women's 60kg event at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, becoming the first Pakistani woman boxer to stand on a Commonwealth Games podium.After her medal-winning campaign, Fatima said the person who inspired her to take up boxing was India's six-time world champion Mary Kom "I am inspired by India's Mary Kom," Fatima told news agency PTI after securing her bronze medal.Born into a poor farming family, Mary Kom overcame financial hardship, social resistance and limited resources to become one of the most successful boxers in history. She secretly trained in her early years while helping her family in the fields before winning six world championship titles, an Olympic bronze medal, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games gold medals, and five Asian Championships.Fatima said the 2014 Bollywood film based on Mary Kom's life became a source of motivation when she started boxing."I used to watch the film made on her life. When I started boxing I used to watch that movie and train. I have a lot of respect for her and inshallah one day I will become like her. I hope I can meet her," Fatima said.Like Mary Kom, Fatima also had to overcome opposition from her family before she could continue with boxing."My background is not that strong. My basic coach taught me everything," she said, as quotes by PTI."My family was against boxing. They would not let me go for training but I fought with them and continued training."She said her family's attitude has changed completely over the years."And now they are more tense than me for my fight and competition," she said with a smile.Fatima hopes her medal will encourage more girls in Pakistan to take up sport and follow their dreams."I was also just another girl. I joined boxing, trained and worked hard. I want other girls who are told to work at home to come out like me."
Article Summary: Fatima Zahra is Pakistan's first female Commonwealth Games boxing medallist. The 22-year-old won a bronze medal in the women's 60kg event in Glasgow. Fatima said the person who inspired her to take up boxing was India's Mary Kom.

The photo capped off a big summer for Haaland, who finished third in scoring at the 2026 FIFA World Cup and led Norway to its first-ever quarterfinal appearance before the team fell to England.Erling Haaland posted a photo with Michael Jordan this past Friday, and the internet immediately started arguing about who looked taller in the frame. The Norwegian striker, still riding the high of a standout 2026 FIFA World Cup run, kept the caption simple: "No caption needed." He let the picture do the talking instead.In the image, Haaland has his arm draped around Jordan's shoulder as both men smile for the camera. Both wore sunglasses and matching shorts, with Haaland in a black perforated polo and Hermès sandals while Jordan kept it simple in a white tee and sneakers. It's the kind of low-key, off-duty shot that usually wouldn't cause much of a stir. This one did.That's because Haaland, at 6-foot-4 to 6-foot-5, is usually the biggest presence in any room he walks into on a soccer pitch.Next to Jordan, listed at 6-foot-6, he suddenly didn't look like it.Fans on X noticed right away. One user, @BurmonSachindev, wrote: "How tall is he?? Article Title: A love that waited 7 years ended in 1 month: Army major returns home draped in Tricolour
Article Text:
Major Hamza Arif had married his Hindu engineer partner just one month prior





JAISALMER: What was meant to be the beginning of a lifetime together turned into an unimaginable tragedy for Major Hamza Arif and his young bride.After spending seven years in a committed relationship and finally convincing their families to accept their marriage, the couple had tied the knot only a month ago.Before the henna on his wife's hands had even faded, fate dealt a devastating blow.Late on Thursday night, Major Hamza Arif lost his life in a horrific road accident near Jaisalmer Military Station when the Tata Safari SUV he was driving collided with a camel and overturned several times.With his death, the dreams and hopes his wife had cherished for their new life together were shattered forever.The couple had recently begun their married life with great optimism.Major Hamza had purchased a new Tata Safari SUV, and his family in Indore had already begun preparations for a grand wedding reception planned for December, when the newlyweds were expected to visit home. Instead of returning to celebrate, the young Army officer is now making his final journey wrapped in the Indian Tricolour.Photographs from the couple's wedding have gone viral on social media, capturing moments of joy, hope and togetherness.The images have deeply moved people, highlighting the heartbreaking contrast between their recent happiness and the tragedy that followed.Major Hamza Arif is survived by his parents and three sisters.He was the only son of a middle-class Bohra Muslim family, and his untimely death has left the family devastated.According to his childhood friend Aman Shukla of Indore, Major Hamza was a native of Dhanvantri Nagar, Indore.He completed his Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering from Chameli Devi College in 2016.Determined to serve the nation, he cleared the selection process and joined the Indian Army in 2017.Through dedication, discipline and exceptional service, he earned three promotions within just nine years, rising to the rank of Major. He was serving at Jaisalmer Military Station at the time of the accident.The fatal crash occurred around 12:30am on Thursday night, nearly 8 kilometres from Jaisalmer city, when the SUV suddenly struck a camel on the road inside the Army area.The impact was so severe that the vehicle overturned four to five times, leaving Major Hamza critically injured.Two other officers travelling with him, Lieutenant Ayushman Gusain and Lieutenant Abhinav Rathore, also sustained injuries.All three were rushed to the Army Hospital, where doctors declared Major Hamza dead. The two injured officers continue to receive treatment.Another childhood friend, Navneet Hardia, said the tragedy has left everyone in shock, noting that Major Hamza had only recently married his longtime partner, an engineer from a Hindu family, after a seven-year relationship.The couple had faced considerable challenges in persuading their families to accept their union before finally solemnising their marriage through a court marriage just a month ago."The family had been eagerly waiting for the couple to come home in December and had already started planning a grand reception," he said. "No one could have imagined that instead of welcoming the newlyweds, they would be receiving Hamza's mortal remains wrapped in the national flag."Friends said Major Hamza's wife had looked forward to building a happy life with her husband and supporting him through his Army career. Those dreams have now been cruelly cut short. Overwhelmed with grief, she is accompanying his mortal remains to Indore for his final journey.Major Hamza had recently purchased the Tata Safari SUV involved in the accident and was driving it himself when the tragedy occurred.The accident has plunged Jaisalmer Military Station and Indore into mourning. Fellow officers, soldiers, friends and relatives have remembered Major Hamza as a dedicated Army officer, a compassionate human being and a humble individual who was deeply respected by everyone who knew him.According to family members and local representatives, Major Hamza Arif's mortal remains will be brought to Indore on Saturday, where he will be laid to rest with full military honours in accordance with the traditions of the Indian Army and the religious customs of the Bohra Muslim community.His passing has left behind not only a grieving family but also a young bride whose dreams of a lifetime together were tragically cut short just weeks after their marriage.
Article Summary: Major Hamza Arif lost his life in a horrific road accident near Jaisalmer Military Station. The Tata Safari SUV he was driving collided with a camel and overturned several times. Major Hamza had married his Hindu engineer partner just one month prior to the tragedy. The young Army officer is now making his final journey wrapped in the Indian Tricolour.

Article Title: 'You are a fool to live so openly, Mallya told Nirav before his arrest'
Article Text:
TOI correspondent from London

: Economic fugitive Vijay Mallya invited fellow billionaire Nirav Modi to his multi-million-pound townhouse overlooking Regent's Park where the pair discussed their respective exiles when the latter was living freely in London before his arrest, the final podcast of the "Diamond King", released Friday, claims.A source in the diamond trade who tipped off Telegraph about Nirav's location, leading to his arrest in March 2019, claims in Episode 4: "Mallya and Nirav were in contact... "Mallya told him he was a fool for living so openly and told him he was too exposed, but Nirav didn't listen.""It's possible Mallya's blueprint gave Nirav the confidence he didn't need to hide." But Nirav did not get bail and has been in a London jail for seven years.Despite an Interpol red notice, Nirav "would regularly stop for a cup of coffee at a cafe in Oxford Street where he would sit reading newspapers... where anyone could see him," the source said. However, he started taking precautions later. To avoid being seen in restaurants, he would pay private chefs £200 to £300 per hour to come to his apartment and cook, but they were never of Indian origin, and it was never the same chef twice, the podcast revealed."I don't think he was clever enough to come up with the (Punjab National Bank) scam himself," the source added. The podcast speculates that Nirav has submitted a second asylum case, which is why he has not gone back. Nirav's solicitor Anand Doobay, who Mallya also used, told TOI: "We are not commenting."

The pair discussed their respective exiles when the latter was living freely in London. New Delhi: Hours after a Delhi court acquitted former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in the alleged sexual harassment case filed by women wrestlers, he on Monday termed the allegations against him a 'conspiracy', saying he had always maintained his innocence and had complete faith in the judicial process."I said this was a conspiracy, and if any of the allegations against me are found to be true, I will hang myself. To this day, I've stood by that statement. Today, after almost three years, the court has honourably acquitted me and Vinod," Singh said.He said he had always stood up for people whose rights were violated and expressed happiness over what he described as a victory in the fight for junior athletes."I always stood up for those who were weak, those whose rights were violated. I had complete faith that justice would be done to me, and I never felt guilty. We were fighting for the junior athletes whose rights were being violated, and I am happy that we won that fight," he added.Following the acquittal, Singh received a warm welcome at his residence, where supporters showered him with flower petals. Crackers were also burst outside his residence as supporters celebrated the verdict.His lawyer, Rajiv Mohan, said the defence would comment in detail after receiving a copy of the judgment."The court has not yet received a copy of the order. Once it is received, we can inform on what basis the court arrived at its conclusion. The arguments we presented have been accepted," Rajiv Mohan said.The case stemmed from allegations made by women wrestlers against Singh during his tenure as WFI chief. Delhi Police filed a chargesheet against him in 2023, invoking charges including sexual harassment, assault or criminal force against women, and criminal intimidation.Former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar was also named as a co-accused.Last month, the court had fixed August 3 for pronouncing its judgment in the case.The proceedings were conducted in a closed courtroom.After hearing final arguments from both sides, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwini Panwar reserved the verdict and directed the parties to file written submissions within two weeks.Senior advocate Rebecca John argued on behalf of the complainants, while the defence team, led by advocate Rajiv Mohan and assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, concluded its submissions on June 30.The case arose from an FIR registered by Delhi Police after women wrestlers staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, alleging sexual harassment during Singh's tenure as WFI chief.Delhi Police filed a 1,500-page chargesheet on June 15, 2023, after completing its investigation. The chargesheet invoked Sections 354, 354A, 354D and 506(1) of the Indian Penal Code.During the trial, the court also recorded the statement of a Special Investigation Team (SIT) member on May 12, along with the deposition of the investigating officer.Singh and Tomar had been facing trial over allegations made by women wrestlers from India and abroad, who accused Singh of sexual harassment during his tenure at the helm of the Wrestling Federation of India.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh was acquitted in the alleged sexual harassment case filed by women wrestlers. He said he had always maintained his innocence and had complete faith in the judicial process. The case arose from an FIR registered by Delhi Police after women wrestlers staged a protest at Jantar Mantar.

Article Text: NEW DELHI: Former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief and ex-BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh was showered with flower petals by supporters as he reached his residence on Monday, after a Delhi court acquitted him in the alleged sexual harassment case filed by six women wrestlers.The celebrations unfolded outside Singh's residence, where supporters welcomed him with flower petals following the verdict delivered by Delhi's Rouse Avenue Court.Earlier in the day, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwini Panwar acquitted Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar in the case.The court had reserved its verdict after hearing final arguments last week.The case arose from allegations made by six women wrestlers, following which Delhi Police filed a chargesheet against Singh on June 15, 2023.He had been charged under Sections 354 (assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 354A (sexual harassment), 354D (stalking) and 506 (criminal intimidation) of the Indian Penal Code.In May 2024, the court ordered framing of charges of sexual harassment and criminal intimidation against Singh but discharged him in relation to allegations made by one of the six complainants. The court had also directed that charges be framed against Vinod Tomar.Both Singh and Tomar remained on bail during the trial.The case had drawn nationwide attention in 2023 after leading Indian wrestlers staged protests accusing Singh of sexual harassment and demanding his arrest.

Article Title: Clear and current danger
Article Text:
Open, live electrical boxes on pedestrian pathways

Open junction boxes on public roads





NEW DELHI: With the monsoon season well under way, exposed and naked electrical wires along roadsides and on utility poles remain life-threatening hazards.On Aug 3, 2024, the National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of reports of avoidable deaths due to drowning and electrocution across Delhi-NCR following heavy rain.Two years on and despite the recurring risk every monsoon, exposed electrical infrastructure often goes unattended, with naked live wires posing an immediate threat of electrocution.For once, Delhi could be thankful to the monsoon for not unleashing its full fury.
Article Summary: The National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of reports of avoidable deaths due to drowning and electrocution across Delhi-NCR. Despite the recurring risk every monsoon, exposed electrical infrastructure often goes unattended, with naked live wires posing an immediate threat.

Article Title: Delhi court acquits Brij Bhushan, Vinod Tomar in women wrestlers sexual harassment case
Article Text:
Earlier this year, (L) Vinesh Phogat revealed that she's one of the 6 victims who filed a sexual harassment complaint against Brij Bhushan Singh (R)
