The court has now honourably acquitted me. I am happy and grateful to my lawyers," he said."For now, this is all I can say. I will comment further after going through the court's reasoned order," the ex-BJP MP added.The court had reserved its verdict on Thursday after hearing final arguments in the case.Also read: 'Flower petals, cheers, slogans': Watch Brij Bhushan Singh's grand welcome after acquittal The case stemmed from allegations made by six women wrestlers, following which Delhi Police filed a chargesheet against Singh on June 15, 2023.He was charged under sections 354 (assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 354A (sexual harassment), 354D (stalking) and 506 (criminal intimidation) of the Indian Penal Code.In May 2024, the court ordered the framing of charges of sexual harassment and criminal intimidation against Singh. However, it discharged him in relation to allegations made by one of the six complainants.The court also directed that charges be framed against Vinod Tomar, former assistant secretary of the WFI.Both Singh and Tomar were out on bail during the trial.The case attracted nationwide attention after leading Indian wrestlers staged protests in 2023, accusing Singh of sexual harassment and demanding his arrest.
Article Summary: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar acquitted. The order was passed by additional chief judicial magistrate Ashwini Panwar at Delhi's rouse avenue court. Singh said the court had "honourably" acquitted him and Tomar.

Article Title: How a master of crime fiction keeps plotting novels at 87
Article Text:
The Hindi pocket book has largely receded from public view. But Surender Mohan Pathak continues to thrill — one surprise twist at a time





NEW DELHI: There was a time when Surender Mohan Pathak was everywhere. You could see his books hogging premium space in AH Wheeler railway bookstalls.You would find a fellow traveller on an inter-city bus immersed in a ‘Khoon Ke Aansoo’.Or you could find a ‘Reporter Ki Hatya’ carefully lodged between textbooks in a naughty classroom. Filmmaker Anurag Kashyap once admitted to hungrily consuming them in his youth.“My first edition print run used to be 1 lakh copies those days,” recalls Pathak.Those days are gone. In times of malls and mobiles, pulp fiction has ceased to be our preferred companions on summer afternoons colonising our imagination.But Pathak’s books continue to be more than a passing reference as in ‘Mirzapur’. OTT series ‘Vimal Khanna’, based on his eponymous anti-hero, is streaming on Amazon Prime.In his book-lined study, the writer still devotes six hours a day, scheming tales of intrigue on his laptop. His latest novel, ‘Kahira Connection’, came out last month.Pathak is 87 years and 322 books old. But the writer speaks with the enthusiasm of IPL commentators and the clarity of detectives in mystery novel climaxes.“I am a businessman. My business is writing. I write novels like a carpenter makes chairs, or a halwai makes jalebis,” he says without hesitation, and with honesty.For decades, the bestselling writer submitted hand-written manuscripts. He maintained this practice until his hands started shaking.Pathak also manages significant hearing loss. During the interview, when the hearing aid briefly stops functioning, he responds to handwritten questions.“Majboori hai budhape ki (It’s a compulsion of old age),” he says, changing the battery. But the loss hasn’t dulled his wit.“Sometimes, to enjoy the last word in a family argument, I just take off the aid,” he laughs. Not many know his oeuvre includes 30 joke books.Like his novels, Pathak’s childhood was filled with twists and turns. He was born in Lahore, where his father worked as a stenographer in a British firm.After Partition, the family landed in Shahdara after spending a year in Jalandhar. It was a tough life for refugees.To escape long queues, water had to be filled from public taps by 4am. Pitiless homeowners raised rents to Shylockian levels.For two 7x9 feet rooms, the Pathaks coughed up Rs 50, a princely sum those days.“Following outcry, the govt set up a rent controller’s office. Our rent was scaled down to Rs 25,” he recalls.A summer holiday in Amritsar would change his life. Pathak had read Nirala’s novel, ‘Nirupama’, and Premchand’s ‘Gaban’ in Urdu, a language he comfortably reads.When Pathak told his maternal uncle that he wanted to read more, he willingly provided the lending library fees.Every day, the 15-year-old would trudge 12 kms to and fro for books by top crime writers: Ibn-e-Safi, Kushwaha Kant and others.Decades later, life would take a full circle when Pathak’s blurb was used to promote Safi’s books.Pathak copiously read the maestros: Agatha Christie, Arthur Conan Doyle and James Hadley Chase.His study library also showcases Elmore Leonard and Richard Stark, two old masters of crime. “Legends have an X ingredient,” says Pathak, also the batchmate of ghazal singer Jagjit Singh in DAV College, Jalandhar.His first story was published in ‘Manohar Kahaniyan’ in 1959 and debut novel, ‘Purane Gunah Naye Gunahgar,’ in 1963.“I came to know of my mistakes only after readers pointed them out. I learnt by hit and trial,” he says candidly.The birth of Hind Pocket Books in 1958 created the perfect platform for modestly priced, accessible romantic/social dramas and crime fiction.Gulshan Nanda emerged as the OG of pulp fiction, his romantic novels closely linked to Rajesh Khanna’s rise to superstardom.In crime and detective fiction, Om Prakash Sharma, Ved Prakash Kamboj, Colonel Ranjit (pseudonym) and Pathak took centre stage.The Sunil series, crafted around the fearless investigative journalist Sunil Chakravarty, has birthed 122 Pathak novels.But the writer feels that he will be remembered for Vimal, the razor-sharp runaway from law with goodness in his heart.Pathak says he read Richard Stark’s Parker novels many times.“I wanted to understand how he developed that character,” he says.There are 48 Vimal novels, including ‘Painsath Lakh Ki Dakaity’ (The Rs 65 Lakh Heist), now in its 24th edition, and regarded by many as his best.During his early years in Indian Telephone Industries, where he worked from 1964 to 1998, Pathak wrote only on Sundays.In 1985, the Rajiv Gandhi govt declared a five-day working week for sarkari employees.“I became a weekend writer after that. I would write for 13-14 hours without breaks,” he says.After office hours in Dariyaganj, he would drive to the Press Club of India and go for a walk to India Gate.He would return by 7pm when the bar opened. “I would often be served the evening’s first drink prepared by a gifted Malayali barman who could pour a precise 60ml without help. My quota was three pegs of 100 Pipers whisky,” he recalls.Pathak lived for 48 years in Krishna Nagar colony. Unlike the East Delhi colony, where everybody knew him, it is a different story in Noida’s Sector 93, where he moved for family reasons in 2012.Sometimes his daily routine of tapping away at his laptop breaks when an unusual fan arrives, like the day a few years back when (then) Polish ambassador Adam Burakowski visited him. “I want to write 24 hours a day,” Pathak says.But, as his favourite protagonist Vimal might declare, life doesn’t always unfold the way we want.
Article Summary: The Hindi pocket book has largely receded from public view. But Surender Mohan Pathak continues to thrill. His latest novel, ‘Kahira Connection’, came out last month. Not many know his oeuvre includes 30 joke books.

Article Title: Scooter hits pothole and skids; woman run over by truck, husband injured
Article Text:
Attachment





Bhiwandi: A 46-year-old woman was killed and her husband injured after their scooter skidded into a pothole on Thane-Bhiwandi Road at Rahanal village on Sunday, throwing them onto the road before the woman was run over by a truck, police said.The deceased was identified as Sunita Akshaylal Pal (46), a resident of Manorama Nagar in Thane. Her husband, Akshaylal Pal, sustained injuries and is undergoing treatment.According to police, the couple was travelling on an Activa scooter towards Anjur Phata in Bhiwandi to inspect a newly purchased flat when the accident occurred. As they were passing through Rahanal village, the scooter hit a large pothole on the concrete road that was filled with rainwater, making it difficult for the rider to gauge its depth.The impact caused the scooter to skid, throwing both riders onto the road. While Akshaylal fell towards the left, Sunita landed on the right side. A truck approaching from behind allegedly ran over her before it could stop, killing her on the spot.On receiving information, a team from Narpoli police station rushed to the spot and conducted a panchnama. The body was sent to Bhiwandi sub-district IGM hospital for post-mortem examination.Police have registered a case and are investigating the circumstances surrounding the accident.The incident has once again brought the poor condition of roads in Bhiwandi and its surrounding areas into focus. Several stretches of Thane-Bhiwandi Road and adjoining roads have developed large potholes despite being concretised. During the monsoon, these potholes remain submerged under rainwater, making them virtually invisible to motorists and increasing the risk of accidents.Local residents and the victim's relatives blamed the civic authorities for failing to repair the dangerous potholes despite repeated complaints. They demanded immediate repairs to the damaged road stretches and sought financial assistance for the bereaved family, warning that more lives could be lost if the hazardous conditions are not addressed without delay.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Sunita Akshaylal Pal (46), a resident of Manorama Nagar in Thane. The couple was travelling on an Activa scooter towards Anjur Phata in Bhiwandi to inspect a newly purchased flat.

Article Title: How Bhiwandi’s ‘Spidey Bhai’ spun a million-strong following
Article Text: MUMBAI: The year was 2016. Shadab Momin was wiping the floor at the juice centre where he worked when the unthinkable happened. His ex-girlfriend walked in. Her brother asked for a one-litre Cola.Momin, hands still sticky from the day’s shift, stopped mopping, handed him the bottle and refused to look at the woman who had become his past. “That night,” says the 28-year-old, “I decided I had to become someone people would bow down to.”Today, in Bhiwandi, few call him Shadab. To the powerloom town, he is Spidey Bhai.With over a million Instagram followers and a part Marvel, part mohalla aura, Momin has become an unlikely symbol for a town better known for flooded roads, crumbling infrastructure and powerloom distress.Like Peter Parker, who grew up not in glossy Manhattan but working-class Queens, Momin came of age amid Bhiwandi’s potholes and poverty. He grew up in Chator Gully, where every Ramzan the aroma of dry fruit-rich gawla mingles with shawarma smoke, and still calls his government school “Peeli school” — the yellow school.Dance came naturally. Money did not. After Class XII, financial troubles forced him to quit studies.Two of his three elder brothers left for Gulf jobs while Momin spent four years at a juice centre. A stint in pharmaceutical sales followed, but by 2018 he knew he was chasing a future that would never quite arrive. “I would grow by two to five per cent every year. That’s it.”His thoughts kept returning to Spider-Man. “In the movies, he was an ordinary boy who entertained people and helped people. I wanted to be that.” It would take another six years, spanning a pandemic and a plateauing pharma career, before Shadab became Instagram’s “Aapka apna Spider-Man”.On April 14, 2024 (”I remember it was Ambedkar Jayanti”), he donned a Rs 2,000 Spider-Man costume bought online and danced in a local market. Trolls arrived first. “Spider-Man should be admitted to hospital,” one wrote. Then came followers. Soon, his unemployed desi Spider-Man sold paan, worked at the juice centre, hauled cement sacks and increasingly filmed himself helping others — distributing food, assisting strangers and turning everyday kindness into content. “Some videos are for entertainment, some for emotion and some for helping.” Within two years he crossed a million followers. Critics called it performative. “Dikhawa nahi hai,” he insists. “They are not for reel. They are for real.”During the monsoon, when floodwater swallows roads, Momin rides to the worst-hit stretches on his scooter carrying little more than a floor wiper. He warns motorists about submerged craters, pushes stranded vehicles and recently went viral for carrying two children through waist-deep water. “Ek saal se sau saal,” he says proudly of his fanbase. He recalls helping rescue passengers from a car trapped in a flooded pothole and spending hours alongside a policeman clearing water. “With great waterlogging comes great responsibility,” read one Instagram comment.These days, Spidey Bhai has been watching Tom Holland ’s latest Spider-Man film and fighting villains that are less cinematic: garbage, potholes and waterlogging. “The authorities are doing their best,” he says. “Still, I don’t understand why the same places flood every year,” adds Momin who wants litterers fined.Every day, on returning home, he washes his sole costume by hand. People do not yet bow to him but they do stop for selfies. Children shout his name and somewhere, perhaps, the ex might have noticed too. Does she follow him online? “I don’t know,” he says. “She is married now.”
Article Summary: Shadab Momin has over a million Instagram followers and a part Marvel, part mohalla aura. The 28-year-old has become an unlikely symbol for a town better known for flooded roads, crumbling infrastructure and powerloom distress. He grew up in Chator Gully, where every Ramzan the aroma of dry fruit-rich gawla mingles with shawarma smoke.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:
Khopoli police arrested four burglars for stealing silver items from a historic temple





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.

Article Title: Man booked for sexually assaulting and injuring stray dog in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Unidentified man booked for sexually assaulting female stray dog (Representative image generated using AI)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 31-year-old woman advocate, who is a dog lover, has registered an FIR at Ulwe police station against an unidentified man aged 30-35 years for allegedly sexually assaulting a female stray dog and causing injury to her private part.The incident occurred outside a tea shop on the ground floor in Siddhivinayak Platinum society in sector 23, Ulwe on Sunday around 11.45pm.Acting on a complaint by Advocate Gayatri Khanvilkar, a resident of the said building, the unidentified accused was booked under BNS section and Prevention of Cruelty to Animal.Adv Khanvilkar said, "As per my daily routine, on Sunday night, I went downstairs to feed the stray dogs loitering near our building. It was raining heavily and pitch darkness due to defunct streetlight poles.""I pucker whistled to call the dogs, when a female stray dog, who had delivered puppies last month, came out from behind a plastic table kept horizontally lying on the floor outside the closed tea shop next to the building's main gate. I could see a man hiding behind the table. I became suspicious and asked him what he was doing.""The man ran away semi-naked with his trouser and underwear in his hand.I chased him but taking advantage of the darkness amid heavy rains, he escaped towards the highway."She added, "I called my father downstairs after informing about the incident. We closely checked the dog and found her bleeding from private part. Also, there was human semen on the floor behind the table. I fed the dog and contacted a volunteer of an NGO Jeevan Foundation Yuva Sena, Animal Welfare Force in Kharghar.""I arranged a cab for the volunteer, who took the injured dog to Panvel Panchayat Samiti's Animal Husbandry department, opposite Panvel ST bus depot, where the government veterinarian confirmed sexual assault on the dog, who was treated for the injuries. Hence, I registered an FIR against the unidentified accused man for sexually assaulting the female stray dog and causing injury to her private part.""Our building's CCTV footage shows the accused man running away from the building, but just because the street lights were not working, his image was not clearly visible. We are retrieving more CCTV footages from other shops in our building for providing them to Ulwe police."PSI Rama Dhavare of Ulwe said, "After registering an FIR, the forensic team collected the human semen sample and hair strands from the crime scene. Once the accused is arrested, the DNA match will be the vital evidence in court for conviction of the accused."
Article Summary: The incident occurred outside a tea shop on the ground floor in Siddhivinayak Platinum society in sector 23, Ulwe on Sunday around 11.45pm. The unidentified accused was booked under BNS section and Prevention of Cruelty to Animal.

Article Title: 9 woman rescued from flesh trade in Taloja lodge, 3 accused held
Article Text:
The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.

NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja and rescued nine women from the flesh trade on July 18. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.Gajanan Kadam, senior inspector of AHTU said, "As per the information received about prostitution being carried out at Hotel Abode Inn Lodging and Boarding in Taloja, we set a trap by sending a decoy customer, whom the lodge manager provided a woman for sexual favour for Rs 3,000 that was accepted by one waiter. On the signal of the customer customer, we raided the lodge, where 9 women were kept for prostitution. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested for dragging the women into prostitution. An FIR was registered at Taloja police station against the three arrested accused Gowda, Pujari and Patil, who were booked relevant BNS sections and Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act. The Panvel court remanded them to police custody till July 21. The rescued women were sent to women's shelter home as directed by the magistrate."
Article Summary: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested.

Article Title: Truck driver arrested from Gujarat for killing fellow driver with iron rod over caste dispute in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Taloja police have caught a truck driver involved in the tragic murder of a fellow driver during a dispute fueled by caste discrimination (Representative image)

NAVI MUMBAI: Taloja police have arrested a 40-year-old truck driver who had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod in the truck parking lot of Nisha Transport company in Nitlas village near Taloja industrial area in Panvel taluka on July 14 early morning.The accused was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday, while he was escaping by train to his home town in UP.The arrested accused has been identified as Ramesh Kumar Yadav and the murder victim as Chandan Pandey, both hailing from UP.Sagar Nikam, PI (crime) of Taloja said, "The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP. The accused Yadav had fatally assaulted the victim Pandey as the latter being a Brahmin used to humiliate Yadav from OBC by treating him as inferior, as claimed by the accused Yadav."PI Nikam informed, "On Monday night, an argument has ensued between Pandey and Yadav in the parking lot over caste discrimination. As they quarrelled, the other truck drivers intervened and resolved the matter. On Tuesday around 5.30 am, again both of them quarrelled, when Yadav assaulted on Pandey's head with an iron rod that proved fatal.""Pandey escaped after threatening other truckers if they attempted to catch him. The security guard Mohammad Alam Hajif-ul Khan (58) informed the police. Pandey was rushed to Panvel sub-district hospital where he was declared brought dead. Subsequently, a murder case was registered against the accused Yadav. His photograph found in his parked truck was immediately circulated to the GRP and RPF at railway stations where multiple trains heading to UP halt.""On Friday, the Valsad GRP informed us that Yadav has been detained at Valsad railway station while he was travelling in an express train to escape to his hometown in UP. Our police team reached Valsad and arrested Yadav. The Panvel JMFC court has remanded Yadav to police custody untill July 21."
Article Summary: Ramesh Kumar Yadav, 40, was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday. He had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod. The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP.

Article Title: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi
Article Text:
Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi (Representational Image)

NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai crime branch unit-2 team has arrested a murder accused from Bhiwandi while conducting a parallel probe in the murder case registered at NRI Coastal police station on Friday after an unidentified man's body with head injuries was found on the pavement near D-Mart in sector 15, Belapur on Friday around 1 am.The arrested accused has been identified as Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.Anil Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-2 informed that, during the probe, when inquired with some rag pickers in the locality, we got an eye witness, who knew Ansari and had seen him assaulting Shaikh with a wooden stick on Thursday night as a quarrel broke out between them after they together consumed liquor near the pavement.The eye witness told that Ansari would pick up rags during day and would spend night where ever he found empty gala or incomplete under construction bldg in Belapur and his father resided in Bhiwandi.Using technical expertise and informer network Ansari was apprehended from Bhiwandi within 24 hours. Thereafter, the murder victim's identity was revealed by him.SPI Patil said, "Ansari claimed that Shaikh was habitual of abusing others after getting drunk. On Thursday night, after the liquor session, Shaikh turned violent without being provoked and attempted to assault him with an iron rod after pushing him to the ground. Hence, he confronted Shaikh by assaulting him with a wooden stick on his head. Seeing Shaikh bleeding profusely and fallen unconscious, he escaped to Bhiwandi. "
Article Summary: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi. Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.

Article Title: 72-Year-Old Woman Found Critical Beside Decomposed Body Of Son
Article Text:
Nagpur:





In a heart-wrenching incident that left residents of Kamptee in shock, a 72-year-old woman was found in a critical state beside the decomposed body of her 50-year-old son in a hut near Ramabai railway crossing on the outskirts of Nagpur. The son, Suresh Bawane, is likely to have died at least 72 hours ago.The matter came to light on Sunday after a neighbour alerted the police about a strong stench coming from the house. When a patrolling constable reached the spot, he witnessed the woman lying helplessly on a cot laid adjacent to another cot on which her son was found dead. He immediately informed the New Kamptee police station, and a team rushed to the location.Locals said the woman, Lakshmi Bawane, looked extremely weak, unable to make any sound or call for help. “She was rushed to a hospital in a critical condition,” said sub-inspector Akshay Jhagde, who was present at the spot.Police said the woman could have collapsed soon had she not been rescued on time. Suresh, who ran an ironsmith shop in Kamptee, was alcoholic and suffered from acute jaundice, said sources. The body was sent for autopsy to the rural hospital in Kamptee.The police were in the process of registering an accidental death case at the time of filing this report. The incident sparked concern over the living conditions and isolation faced by elderly people in the area, said sources.
Article Summary: A 72-year-old woman was found in a critical state beside the decomposed body of her son. The son, Suresh Bawane, is likely to have died at least 72 hours ago. The matter came to light on Sunday after a neighbour alerted the police about a strong stench coming from the house.

Article Title: Futala’s Banyan Tree Set To Become Nagpur’s New Night-Time Landmark
Article Text:
Futala Banyan Tree

Nagpur:





The towering artificial banyan tree taking shape at Futala Lake is set to become Nagpur’s newest night-time landmark, serving as the centrepiece of the revived musical fountain.Speaking exclusively to TOI, Emmy Award-winning cinematographer and technical director of the Futala Musical Fountain project, Alphonse Roy, said the tree has been conceived as the visual heart of the attraction rather than merely a stage prop.“Everything revolves around the tree. It is the central projection surface as well as the visual identity of the project,” Roy said.Unlike conventional projection surfaces, the tree’s complex geometry has required months of planning before animation work could begin. Standing 15 metres high and 30 metres long, the structure, with its intricate network of branches, will undergo a detailed LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) scan before being covered with specially designed projection fabric.The LiDAR survey is being carried out by a Nagpur-based geospatial team. Once the front section facing the viewing gallery is covered, the structure will undergo a second scan.“We first scan the exact contours of the structure. Based on those measurements, the visual content is generated so that every animation matches the geometry of the tree perfectly,” Roy said.Project officials are targeting Aug 20 to complete installation of the front projection fabric, after which work will begin on the rear section before the second round of scanning.According to Roy, the projection fabric has been engineered to achieve an optimum balance of 76% reflectance and 24% translucence. The high reflectance ensures bright, sharp projection mapping, while the controlled translucence allows integrated LED and ROBE lighting concealed inside the tree to glow after the shows conclude.Lighting is also being customised for the project. High-performance ROBE fixtures and LEDs will be installed only after part of the projection fabric is in place, allowing engineers to determine the precise position of each light.“We cannot place the lights blindly. They have to be positioned to achieve the best possible illumination while ensuring they are not obstructed by poles or other fountain equipment. The objective is to eliminate shadows and create a seamless visual effect,” Roy said.The team is continuing to test different colour temperatures, brightness levels and lighting combinations to create the desired ambience.“The idea is not just to illuminate the tree but to create a unique night-time character. Every effect has to complement the projections, the water and the overall atmosphere,” he said.Even after the fountain shows end each evening, the tree will remain illuminated through its integrated LED system, giving Futala a permanent visual signature. Owing to its scale, the illuminated structure is expected to be visible from aircraft approaching or departing Nagpur.“We want the tree to become something people instantly associate with Nagpur. It should remain a landmark even when the show is over,” Roy said.With structural work progressing steadily and digital mapping scheduled later this month, the artificial banyan tree is steadily transforming into what its creators hope will become the defining visual icon of the revamped Futala lakefront.
